Russian Military Lieutenant Colonel Reportedly Killed in Car Blast in St. Petersburg — A Russian military lieutenant colonel was killed and his wife seriously injured in a car blast in St. Petersburg on Thursday, according to Russian media. Investigators confirmed one death and opened a criminal probe, but described the incident as a vehicle fire.

EU States Push to Revive Russian-Asset ‘Reparations Loan’ for Ukraine — EU countries are pushing Brussels to revive a stalled plan to use frozen Russian assets to fund Ukraine, as Kyiv faces a €23.1 billion defense funding gap. Sweden, the Netherlands, Spain, and Poland are urging the European Commission to find ways around Belgium’s opposition to the proposed “reparations loan.”

Inside Kherson’s Red Zone: A Kyiv Post Special Report — Inside Kherson’s Red Zone, Kyiv Post takes you to one of Ukraine’s most dangerous civilian environments, where drones stalk streets, artillery crosses the Dnipro, and residents refuse to abandon their homes. Journalist Korbinian Leo Kramer spent more than two weeks documenting life on the front line and the people who endure it.

Russian Army Chief Visits Troops on Ukraine Front — Russia’s army chief Valery Gerasimov said Russian forces are advancing toward Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, claiming they are just four kilometers from the city’s outskirts. The Kremlin has vowed to seize all of Donetsk as fighting intensifies and US-brokered peace talks remain stalled.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Ozon Logistics Hubs in Russia as Marketplace Warehouses Come Under Sustained Attack — Ukrainian drones struck Ozon logistics facilities in Ufa and Orenburg overnight on Thursday, Aug. 27, disrupting operations at Russia’s second-largest online marketplace. The strikes come amid a widening campaign targeting major e-commerce warehouses, with billions of rubles in potential losses reported.

Kyiv Endures Hours-Long Russian Drone Assault as Drones Fall in City Center — Russia launched a fresh drone attack on Kyiv Thursday, just hours after an overnight missile-and-drone barrage. Around a dozen attack drones targeted the capital, triggering air defense fire and explosions. Fires were reported at Kyiv’s Lobanovskyi Stadium and in the Holosiivskyi District as residents sheltered underground.

CIA Chief Warned Putin Against NATO Attack During Surprise Moscow Visit – Reports — CIA Director John Ratcliffe secretly traveled to Moscow this week to warn Vladimir Putin against attacking NATO, The Wall Street Journal and Politico reported. The warning reportedly focused on the Baltic states, amid US intelligence concerns that Russia could seek to “test NATO’s resolve” with a limited attack.

How Russia Finds the Cracks in American Society – and Widens Them — Russia has a well-developed playbook for influence operations through propaganda. Laura Loomer got sucked into one of those operations, but she eventually realized what happened and is now exposing how Moscow works.

EXPLAINER: The Birth of an Independent Ukrainian Press: From Samvydav to Modern Journalism — Before Ukraine’s independence, uncensored journalistic ideas travelled through hidden networks of typed manuscripts, unofficial newspapers, and foreign radio broadcasts. Radio Liberty and a new generation of journalists then helped to loosen Soviet control, connect Ukraine’s regions and prepare the ground for a more modern independent press – one that emerged before 1991 and would soon face the hard test

53 Ukrainians Missing After Nepal-Tibet Disaster, Second Flood Feared — At least 53 Ukrainians are missing after catastrophic floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 165 people and left more than 1,000 unaccounted for. The US Geological Survey says a glacial collapse triggered the disaster, while experts warn an upstream blockage could cause a second flood.

Russian Barrage Hits Kyiv, Sets Warehouses Ablaze in Latest Overnight Attack — Russia launched a coordinated overnight attack on Kyiv using ballistic missiles and drones, triggering explosions across the capital. Debris fell in the Podilskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts, while the broader barrage also struck Odesa, Kryvyi Rih, and Zaporizhzhia, injuring civilians.

Did CIA Chief Warn Moscow Against NATO Attack – or Discuss Iran-Russia Ties? — CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s unannounced visit to Moscow has fueled speculation over its purpose, with the most prominent theory being that he warned Russia against testing or attacking NATO. Trump called the trip “semi-routine,” while the Kremlin said Ratcliffe did not meet Putin. A less-discussed possibility is that talks touched on Russia-Iran cooperation.

Russian Drone Strikes on Kherson Injure 4, Including Child — Two Russian drone attacks struck separate districts of Kherson on Aug. 26, injuring three adults and a 10-year-old boy. The child was hospitalized in moderate condition after a drone struck a car in the Korabelnyi district.

France Warns of New Hybrid Threat After Leipzig Drone Attack — France’s domestic intelligence chief says an explosives-laden drone apparently targeting a Ukrainian military supply aircraft in Germany signals a growing risk of more violent hybrid attacks in Europe. French officials are particularly concerned about threats to defense, technology, energy and communications infrastructure.

US Senator Says ‘Sledgehammer’ Russia Sanctions Could Pass House Next Month — US Senator Richard Blumenthal said he hopes sweeping sanctions targeting Russia will pass the House of Representatives next month, calling the legislation a “sledgehammer” against Moscow’s ability to finance its war in Ukraine.

53 Ukrainian Nationals Missing in Nepal Flash Flood That Killed At Least 160 — Fifty-three Ukrainian nationals, including a group of 46 tourists, are reported missing after a flash flood struck villages in Nepal, near the country’s border with China. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said its embassies in India and China are coordinating with local authorities as searches continue.

Russia’s Mobilization Looming as Putin Sticks to Ambitions — Russia insists that no new mobilization is planned, despite nationwide readiness exercises and Ukrainian warnings that Vladimir Putin could call up 300,000 troops after September’s parliamentary elections. The denials come as Russia’s paid recruitment system struggles to generate net manpower, its Donbas offensive produces diminishing territorial returns, and the country’s remaining liquid fiscal reserve falls below its accumulated 202

Russia May Escalate Strikes on Ukraine, Kremlin Sources Say — Russia is considering intensifying ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine amid stalled peace negotiations, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, Aug. 26, citing Kremlin-linked sources. Moscow reportedly sees further escalation as one of its few remaining ways to pursue its military aims.

Belarus Builds Military Rail Link Near Ukraine Border — Belarus is building rail infrastructure near Yakimivka in the Gomel region, near its border with Ukraine. Kyiv has said it is monitoring the project – which could receive military trains and unload heavy equipment – though no troop movements have been detected.

Trump Says US ‘Working Very Hard’ to End War in Ukraine Amid CIA Chief’s Visit to Moscow — US President Donald Trump said Wednesday, Aug. 26, that CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s trip to Moscow could produce results as Washington seeks to end Russia’s war against Ukraine. Meanwhile, the Kremlin said Ratcliffe did not meet Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Hungary Formally Classifies Russia a ‘Threat’ in UN Document — Led by Prime Minister Péter Magyar, Hungary’s new government officially classified Russia as a “threat” in a document submitted for the United Nations (UN) General Assembly, marking a sharp break from its previous Kremlin-aligned policy under former PM Viktor Orbán.

Polish President Wishes Ukraine Victory in War With Russia, Zelensky Publishes Letter — Polish President Karol Nawrocki sent President Volodymyr Zelensky a letter marking Ukraine’s 35th anniversary of independence, in which he wished Ukraine victory in its war with Russia and the restoration of its territorial integrity within internationally recognized borders. Zelensky later published the letter and said Ukraine would remember Poland’s support while emphasizing the need to develop relations ba

Ukrainian Military Adds Jet-Powered 'Alexa Spatium' Interceptor Drones to Its Arsenal — Ukraine’s defense ministry unveiled its new “Alexa Spatium” drone but remained tight-lipped about its performance. It said the drone can be equipped with different warheads, with TV and infrared guidance, without losing its ability to be controlled remotely by operators. It also shared footage of its catapult launches.

Drone Washes Up on Beach Near Bulgaria's Varna, Navy Sappers Called In — A drone measuring about 2 meters long and 1.5 meters wide washed ashore at Kabakum beach near Varna, Bulgaria, on Wednesday, Aug. 26, Bulgarian broadcaster BNT reported. Navy sappers cordoned off the area and began securing the device, which initial information suggested posed no danger.

Norway Pledges $9.2 Billion to Ukraine for 2027: With Most Going to Military — Norway will give Ukraine 85 billion kroner ($9.2 billion) in 2027, the same amount it committed for 2026, Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre told Norwegian broadcaster NRK. Of the total, most is earmarked for military aid, with a smaller portion for civilian support.

Ratcliffe Visits Moscow — With Russia refusing to negotiate in earnest and helping Iran against the US, CIA director John Ratcliffe traveled to Moscow. The unexpected visit was intended to cool the rapidly overheating engine driving the world to all-out war.

Russia Risks Losing 2 More Starlink Alternative Satellites — Two of Russia’s Rassvet satellites – the country’s answer to the US’s Starlink – are falling and risk burning up in the atmosphere, according to a cosmonaut researcher. Intelligence suggests that Russia aims to put 292 satellites in orbit by 2027 – while the number falls short of Starlink’s over 7,800 in orbit, analysts warned that the existing few dozen still provide regular albeit brief coverage over Ukraine.

Belarus Orders Surprise Military Readiness Check as CIA Chief Visits Moscow — Belarus has ordered a surprise military readiness check as CIA Director John Ratcliffe visits Moscow for unannounced intelligence contacts. The exercise will deploy a brigade from its permanent base and test combat capabilities, including strikes against a potential enemy, amid growing concerns over Russia’s military plans and Belarus’ role in the war.

China Helps Russia Upgrade Shaheds Into a New Threat for Ukraine — China has emerged as a key supplier of components for Russia’s increasingly sophisticated Shahed drones. New turbojet-powered variants can reach 483 km/h, making them harder for Ukraine to intercept, increasing pressure on its limited air-defense resources.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Military Network, Hitting Radar, Drone Center, Key Supply Depots — Ukrainian Defense Forces struck several Russian military targets on Aug. 25 and overnight into Aug. 26, including a Kasta radar station in occupied Crimea, a drone training center in Luhansk, a repair and recovery base in occupied Crimea, and multiple fuel, equipment and ammunition depots. Ukrainian forces also hit a ground relay used to control Geran and Gerbera drones in occupied Crimea.

Why Was the CIA Chief in Moscow? — CIA Director John Ratcliffe made an unannounced visit to Moscow for talks with Russian intelligence officials. The purpose remains unclear, with analysts suggesting Iran, Ukraine, prisoner exchanges, or security concerns. European media say the unusually public visit may signal either diplomatic maneuvering or worsening US-Russia tensions requiring confidential communication.

Remembering Our Heroes — As Ukraine fills its towns and villages with portraits of fallen defenders, Russia promotes military service while invoking Orthodox symbols and relics to support its war effort. From memorial avenues to the destruction of Russian Orthodox relics sent to occupied Donbas, the war has reshaped how both countries commemorate sacrifice, heroism, and death.

Seven Dead, Nine Missing After Fire at Russia-China Gas Complex — A fire at Russia’s Amur Gas Chemical Complex killed seven people, including six Chinese nationals, while nine Chinese workers remain missing. The under-construction facility treated 152 injured people, with 36 hospitalized. Authorities are investigating potential safety violations as the Sibur-Sinopec project deepens Russia-China industrial cooperation.

EXPLAINER: Ukraine’s Free Media at 35 – What You Need to Know — On the 35th anniversary of Ukraine’s independence, Kyiv Post launches a special series tracing the rise of a free Ukrainian press – from underground publications and Soviet censorship to investigative journalism and wartime reporting. The series explores how media freedom became a cornerstone of Ukraine’s sovereignty, democracy and national resilience.

Zelensky Awards Elon Musk Ukraine’s Order of Freedom — President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded Elon Musk Ukraine’s Order of Freedom by decree on Aug. 26, citing the American entrepreneur’s personal contributions to protecting human life and freedom and developing relations between the Ukrainian and American peoples.

Kremlin Says CIA Chief Did Not Meet Putin During Moscow Visit — CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow for contacts between US and Russian intelligence services but did not meet President Vladimir Putin, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said. The unexpected visit prompted speculation that the discussions could have involved the war in Ukraine, a potential energy and port strike moratorium, or US intelligence on Russia’s military plans.

Ukrainian Military-Grade Drone Detector ‘Chuika’ Now Available to Civilians — Ukraine’s military-grade “Chuika 3.0” drone detector is now available for civilian purchase, offering frontline residents a way to detect Russian FPV drones from up to 4 kilometers away. The device, already used by Ukraine’s Defense Forces, can warn users before an approaching drone becomes visible.

Russia, Ukraine Preparing Another ‘Quite Big’ POW Exchange, Russian State Media Says — Russia and Ukraine are preparing another major prisoner exchange, Russian state media reported Wednesday, days after swapping 103 captives each. The announcement follows an unannounced Moscow visit by CIA Director John Ratcliffe, though no link between his talks and the planned swap has been confirmed.

Putin Signs Three Secret Decrees as CIA Chief Makes Surprise Moscow Visit — Russian President Vladimir Putin signed three undisclosed decrees on Aug. 25, coinciding with CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s surprise Moscow visit and a US request for Ukraine to pause strikes on Moscow and St. Petersburg. The contents of the decrees remain unknown.

4-Year-Old Girl and Woman Killed as Russian Drones Strike Chernihiv — A Russian drone strike on Chernihiv killed a 4-year-old girl and a 49-year-old woman and injured a 14-year-old girl. Ukraine’s Air Force said Russia launched 162 attack and decoy drones overnight, with 134 neutralized.

Wildberries Hub, Major Refinery Hit Overnight as Russia Reports 426 Drones — A massive overnight drone barrage reportedly targeted a Wildberries logistics hub and Lukoil’s major Kstovo refinery. Russia claimed 426 drones were downed, while a separate strike in Lipetsk region reportedly killed 2 people.

35 on 35 – Independent Ukraine Through the Eyes of a Ukrainian Woman — As Ukraine marks its 35th year as an independent nation, a woman born just a few months before the country adopted its declaration of independence tells Kyiv Post how her life unfolded as the country found its footing.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 25, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on August 25, 2026.

South Korea Says Russian Military Planes Entered Its Air Defense Zone — South Korea scrambled fighter jets after multiple Russian military aircraft entered its air defense zone over the East Sea, though they did not violate sovereign airspace.

Putin’s New Decree Makes Russian Businesses Pay for Failing to Stop Ukrainian Drones — Putin’s new decree shifts more wartime responsibility onto Russian businesses, allowing the state to take control if owners fail to protect or quickly restore critical infrastructure.

In Izyum, Young Ukrainians Fight to Keep a Battered City Alive as Russian Forces Close In — In Izyum, residents are trying to preserve normal life and keep the city’s future alive as Russian forces move closer again.

US Asked Ukraine Not to Strike Moscow, St. Petersburg During CIA Chief’s Visit — Washington asked Kyiv to temporarily halt strikes on Moscow and St. Petersburg during CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s visit to Russia, Ukrainian officials confirmed.

Fedorov Says Ukraine Risks ‘Slowly Losing’ War Without Urgent Changes — Former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov says Ukraine risks gradually losing the war unless Kyiv urgently changes strategy and scales new military technologies.

France Seeks Limits on Ukraine’s Non-EU Defense Purchases — France is seeking to limit Ukraine’s ability to use EU-backed funding for defense equipment sourced outside Europe, Euronews reported on Tuesday, Aug. 25. The proposal regards exemptions under the EU’s €90 billion ($105 billion) Ukraine Support Loan, including for Chinese drone parts and US-made Patriot interceptors.

Dolly Parton, Country Music Icon and Philanthropist Who Dedicated 2022 Awards Show to Ukraine, Dies at 80 — Country music icon and philanthropist Dolly Parton has died aged 80 in Nashville, Tennessee. The singer, known for her hits including “Jolene,” “9 to 5” and “I Will Always Love You,” is also remembered for dedicating the 2022 ACM Awards to Ukraine after Russia’s invasion, for her decades of charitable work through the Dollywood Foundation, and as an ambassador for the Sunflower Guitar for

Russian Strikes Injure 35 Across 3 Cities, Including 2-Month-Old Infant — Ukraine’s State Emergency Service reported at least 35 people injured across a series of Russian attacks on Tuesday, Aug. 25. The largest strike hit Kramatorsk, where nine guided aerial bombs (KABs) injured 24 people, including a 2-month-old infant.

KADORR Group’s Ruslan Kivan Receives State Award From Zelensky — KADORR Group chairman and co-founder of KADORR Group LLC, Ruslan Kivan, was awarded the Order of Merit, third class, under a decree signed by President Volodymyr Zelensky as Ukraine marked its 35th Independence Day on Monday, Aug. 24.

Verkhovna Rada Confirms Ukraine Not Considering Mobilizing Women — Ukraine’s parliament, the Verkhovna Rada, issued an official statement saying Ukraine is neither carrying out nor considering the mobilization of women. The statement came after former US presidential envoy Keith Kellogg argued on Monday, Aug. 24, that Ukraine should mobilize women into its Defense Forces because they can fight as effectively as men.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe Visits Moscow, US Media Reports — A US Air Force C-17 military transport plane landed in Moscow on Tuesday, Aug. 25 after flying from Riga, raising questions about the mission. CBS News later reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe was in Moscow for meetings with Russian authorities. Ahead of the trip, Washington reportedly asked Ukraine to temporarily refrain from striking Moscow and St. Petersburg, according to Axious and Suspilne.

Ukraine Receives Additional Patriot Missiles, Zelensky Says — Ukraine has received additional Patriot missiles, President Volodymyr Zelensky said during a meeting with media representatives alongside Estonian President Alar Karis. He also announced additional Crotale air defense systems and missiles, AIM missiles, and confirmation from the UK on SCALP long-range missile production.

Ukraine Tests World's First Purpose-Built Robot Aircraft Carrier for Drones — Ukraine’s 7-meter Magura MV11 is a 2,200-kg-payload mothership designed to launch other drones, expanding the sea-going robot motorboat from a proven warship-killer into probably the world’s first drone “aircraft carrier.”

Ukraine Strikes Deep Inside Russia Despite Starlink Limits — A series of Ukrainian FP-2 drone strikes against radars, air-defense systems and military targets in Russia’s Rostov Oblast has raised questions about how Kyiv maintains real-time control over drones in areas where Starlink is reportedly unavailable. Russian and Western OSINT analysts suggest Ukraine may be using relay drones and mesh networks to maintain connectivity during strikes deep inside Russian territory.

US Military Transport Plane Lands in Moscow After Flight From Riga — A US Air Force C-17 military transport plane landed in Moscow after flying from Riga, triggering questions over the purpose of the unusual flight. The Kremlin says it has no information about the aircraft and denies any planned meetings with US officials this week.

Russia Claims Another Sumy Settlement, Ukraine Calls Novokostiantynivka Capture ‘False’ — Russia claimed it had captured Novokostiantynivka in the Sumy region, but Ukraine rejected the claim. Kyiv says the settlement remains under Ukrainian control and that fighting with Russian forces continues in the area.

Kanye West’s Russia Concerts in Limbo After St. Petersburg Arena Pulls Out — Kanye West’s planned October concerts in St. Petersburg are in doubt after Gazprom Arena abruptly said it never signed a deal to host the US rapper, despite announcing the shows and selling 81,000 tickets in 24 hours. Russian media suggest authorities may have pressured the venue to pull out.

From Diia to Deep Strikes: 4 Ways Ukraine Reinvented Itself Since Independence — Ukraine has transformed since independence, building a digital-government platform used by millions, a massive drone industry and homegrown ballistic missiles. Wartime innovation has also enabled spectacular operations such as the SBU’s 117-drone strike on Russian strategic bombers.

Trump Urges ‘Durable, Lasting Peace’ in Ukraine Independence Day Letter — US President Donald Trump congratulated Ukraine and President Volodymyr Zelensky on the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Ukraine’s independence. In a letter shared by Zelensky, Trump praised Ukrainians for their resilience and said Washington remained confident in Ukraine’s future as a sovereign and prosperous nation.

Kyiv Hosts 6th Summit of First Ladies and Gentlemen on Resilience — Initiated by Ukraine’s First Lady Olena Zelenska, the Sixth Summit of First Ladies and Gentlemen brought together representatives of 14 countries to share experiences of resilience. The summit presented Ukraine’s “Sophiynist” philosophy and the Global Vocabulary of Resilience, bringing together experiences from 38 countries.

British Man Fighting for Russia Killed in Ukraine — Bradley Townsend, a 33-year-old man from Yorkshire, was reportedly killed by a Ukrainian drone near eastern Ukraine’s Lyman in June while fighting for Russian forces. Townsend previously appeared in a video in April after traveling to Russia, appearing alongside other known British fighters.

Ex-Pussy Riot Member Says She Was Forced to Spy for Russia’s FSB — A former Pussy Riot member, Rita Flores, says Russia’s FSB forced her to work as an informant for nearly three years after threatening her family and her safety. She claims she was ordered to spy on activists and artists and help lure Pussy Riot figure Pyotr Verzilov into a suspected kidnapping plot before escaping Russia.

Russia’s Military Missed 15 of Putin’s Deadlines to Seize Donbas, ISW Says — Russian President Vladimir Putin has set the military at least 15 deadlines to fully seize Donbas since the start of the full-scale invasion, but Russian forces have failed to meet any of them, according to ISW.

Verkhovna Rada Summons Fedorov Over 'Midas' Corruption Probe — Ukraine’s former defense minister Fedorov has been summoned to a committee meeting on Aug. 31 to answer questions on defense and corruption following his latest accusation against government institutions.

Ukrainian Basketball Player Leaves LSU After Tigers Sign Russian Athlete — Kyiv-born basketball player Kate Koval is leaving LSU less than two weeks after the Tigers signed 17-year-old Russian center Anna Minaeva, who previously played for a professional club in Moscow. LSU cited “personal reasons” for Koval’s departure, while neither side has publicly linked the move to Minaeva’s signing.

UK PM Burnham Plans US Trip to Push Trump on Ukraine Patriots — UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he plans to travel to the US next month to lobby President Donald Trump to let Ukraine access Patriot air defense missile stocks before winter, Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, Aug. 25. Burnham said European leaders may hold another Coalition of the Willing meeting around the UN General Assembly in New York to secure US interceptors and stocks from other countries. Zelensky has asked for 300 Patriot

Ukraine Сelebrates 35 Years of Independence — Ukraine’s 35 years of independence have brought major democratic and institutional reforms, but often only after public pressure and crises. Current debates over elections and corruption reflect the freedoms Ukraine is defending. Valerii Zaluzhnyi argues that neglecting national defence after 1991 helped enable Russia’s full-scale invasion.

US Again Declines to Join UN Statement Condemning Russia’s Strikes on Ukraine — The US has again refused to join a UN statement condemning Russia’s strikes on Ukraine, as 50 countries called for an immediate ceasefire. The move comes as Kyiv, Washington and European partners work on a new peace framework that could include a ceasefire and troop withdrawals.

Russia’s Deadly Overnight Attack Kills 3, Shuts Key Ukraine-Moldova Border Crossing — A Russian drone attack damaged a Ukraine-Moldova border checkpoint, forcing it to close temporarily. The overnight barrage also targeted four Ukrainian cities and multiple regions, with at least 3 people killed and residential and civilian infrastructure damaged.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Afipsky Refinery for 5th Time, Novoshakhtinsk Plant Reportedly Targeted — On Tuesday, Ukrainian drones hit the Afipsky refinery for the fifth time this year, while the Novoshakhtinsk refinery was reportedly targeted in a separate attack. The attacks come amid mounting disruptions to Russia’s oil-refining and fuel infrastructure.

Former Italian Ambassador Warns Russian Influence Could Shape Italy’s 2027 Election — Former Italian ambassador to Ukraine Pier Francesco Zazo has warned that Russian propaganda still has significant influence in Italy, weakening support for military aid to Kyiv. Speaking in Kyiv, he linked Italian attitudes to the country’s communist legacy, pacifist traditions and weak safeguards against disinformation. Zazo said these factors could benefit pro-Russian parties in Italy’s 2027 election.

Independent Ukraine at 35: A Sober Look Into the Future — Ukraine’s 35th year of independence finds the country fighting not only for survival, but for the shape of its future. The next test will be whether wartime unity can translate into durable reform – bringing veterans and displaced citizens home, rebuilding without corruption, restoring democratic balance, navigating the hard politics of EU accession, and creating a security posture strong enough to deter Russia without sacrificing the fre
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 24, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on August 24, 2026.

Zelensky: Ukraine Can Produce 200–300 Long-Range Drones Daily, With Reach Up to 3,000 Km — Zelensky said Ukraine can produce 200–300 long-range strike drones a day, with weapons ranging from about 350 to 3,000 km, but needs more funding to expand attacks on Russia.

Finland’s Stubb: Deep Strikes Into Russia ‘Only Way’ to Push Moscow Toward Peace Talks — Finnish President Alexander Stubb backed Ukraine’s long-range strikes inside Russia, saying they raise the cost of the war and can help push Moscow toward peace negotiations.

What Did the Coalition of the Willing Agree in Kyiv? — Coalition of the Willing leaders meeting in Kyiv pledged stronger air defenses, increased military and energy support, tougher sanctions on Russia, and continued preparations for a multinational force that could deploy after a ceasefire.

Armenia Signals Break With Russia-Led CSTO as Kremlin Says Yerevan Is ‘Free to Leave’ — Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Yerevan has no plans to return to the Russia-led CSTO and would welcome being expelled from the alliance. The Kremlin responded that Armenia is free to leave, as Yerevan also moves toward a formal EU membership application.

Ukraine’s UN Envoy Demands Action Against Russia’s ‘Ballistic Terror’ at Security Council — Ukraine’s UN Ambassador Andriy Melnyk called for decisive international action against Russia’s escalating ballistic missile campaign, saying Moscow is already losing its war and demanding far-reaching sanctions against Russia’s weapons industry.

Rubio Congratulates Ukraine, Pledges Continued US Security and Economic Ties — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Ukraine on its 35th Independence Day, reaffirming Washington’s commitment to Ukrainian sovereignty, security and economic ties.

Ukraine Allies Defy Moscow Threats, Pledge Air Defense Boost and Missile Production — Ukraine’s allies gathered in Kyiv on Independence Day with air defense at the top of the agenda, pledging continued military support despite mounting Russian threats. Britain also cleared the release of classified information to support Ukrainian production of Storm Shadow/SCALP missiles.
